page: Microsoft Azure L16as_v3 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance based on the AMD EPYC 7763 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores operating at 3.525 GHz with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system features 128.0 GB of memory alongside 4012 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. The virtualization layer is managed by Microsoft Hyper-V, and the configuration contains no discrete hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark measurements indicate strong single-core CPU throughput, with stress-ng reaching 2702.28 to place in the top quartile of evaluated instances, while multi-core stress-ng records 21623.79 within the median bracket. Geekbench multi-core registers at 9888.0 and single-core at 1689.0. Memory bandwidth evaluation shows 1034.94 GB/sec for small cached blocks, whereas large uncached transfers drop to 39.1 GB/sec for read and 22.81 GB/sec for write operations, reflecting hardware memory bus limitations during sustained large-block streaming.

The 4012 GB NVMe SSD volume gives the instance strong local I/O capacity, supported by benchmark throughput of 15.84 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark database score of 7050.46. Combined with an 8 GB per vCPU memory allocation, this server provides efficient resource density for local disk caching and transaction processing without external disk attachments. It is structurally aligned with workloads such as relational databases, NoSQL engines, search indexers, and high-throughput data ingestion pipelines.
description: The Microsoft Azure L16as_v3 is a storage-optimized virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 8 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The platform includes 128.0 GB of memory and 4012 GB of bundled high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor without discrete GPU acceleration. In benchmark evaluations, the instance records strong single-core stress-ng performance alongside balanced multi-core output and 15.84 million Redis SET operations per second, though uncached memory write and read bandwidth sit lower relative to high-tier memory instances. By combining substantial low-latency local NVMe storage capacity with an 8 GB per vCPU memory profile, the L16as_v3 provides a resource-dense configuration well suited for transactional databases, NoSQL clusters, search indices, and large-scale data ingestion workloads.
